sequel

SEE-kwul (stress on SEE) · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Something that comes after an earlier event and grows out of it.

The peace talks were a sequel to the border agreement signed two springs earlier.

Example

The blackout turned out to be a sequel to last winter's storm damage, since the patched power lines finally gave way.

Calling the blackout a sequel says it was not random: it followed the earlier damage in time and grew directly out of it. The word links the two events into one continuing story.

How sequel sits among its neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

follow-up

follow-up: anything that comes as a next step

continuation

continuation: the act of carrying something on further

Antonyms

original

original: the first work or event, before any others followed

opening

opening: the very first part, where things begin

How Strong Is It? — follow-up → sequel → series

follow-up vs. sequel

follow-up vs. sequel: A follow-up is lighter than a sequel: a follow-up can be any small next step, while a sequel is a complete later chapter that grows out of the first.

series vs. sequel

series vs. sequel: A series goes further than a sequel: a sequel adds one continuation to an earlier work or event, but a series strings many of them into a whole connected chain.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sequ

root — sequ: to follow

suffix — el

suffix — el: noun ending

Put it together

Put it together: Start with sequ- ('to follow') and add the noun ending -el: a sequel is literally 'a thing that follows.' That is why it fits any later event that follows from an earlier one, not just the second movie in a series.

Use the root in a new word: sequence

Use the root in a new word: sequence: Follow the sequence of steps in order, because each one builds on the step before it.

Root Check

Word Choice

Sequel is not only for movies and books: historians and reporters use it for any event that follows from an earlier one, as in 'the strike was a sequel to the failed talks.' If the later thing merely comes after without growing out of the first, plain follow-up fits better.
